confirmed: Every retired host epoch requires one exact successful snapshot marker with VM/epoch identity, sequence, and full logical snapshot paths.
Batch numbers and log order must agree on both sides of the marker. The kept prefix starts at batch 1 and has exactly discard_sequence complete mapped/ACK pairs.
The top-level verifier validates all raw API responses as 204 and binds their request bodies before host_epochs uses the unique snapshot call.

A host ACK present in frozen RAM but not yet consumed by the paused guest is retained; restored guest completion can therefore correlate with its old source epoch. Post-cut source ACKs are excluded explicitly, not dropped by GPA guesswork.

The guest parser requires a loss-free sequential submission/completion history with one active batch. Host parser requires contiguous per-epoch mapped/ACK pairs and equal fields. Ordered interval-union comparison then checks exactly the same page sets.
Final host records after a captured guest prefix are labeled tails rather than counted as guest-observed completions. Busy/no-op ACKs are distinguished from discarded ranges.
conservative_limits: An incomplete retired host batch is rejected before applying its snapshot cut, even if that batch lies strictly after the cut and is outside restored state. This is a possible false rejection of safely fenced evidence, not a false success.

host_epochs itself relies on the top-level raw API success validation. It is not a standalone API evidence validator. Additional socket/role and receipt-order binding could be useful hardening, though current unique VM/epoch snapshot paths and native marker identity already constrain matching.
runtime_scope: This is source review only. Formal multi-epoch replay must still run against the completed saved receipts.
